newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures score more gains late on cash.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures score more gains late on cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures continued to score gains late Wednesday in moderately active trade, driven by reports of sharp gains in the cash and some technical buying as prices moved through resistance.
At 1410 EDT, November jumped 14.7 cents to $2.585 per million British thermal units, while December was up the 10-cent limit at $2.705. Others were up by one to 7.3 cents.

"Things are looking pretty strong. A lot of people were caught short this month, but we could see some profit taking before the close," said one Houston-based trader, noting some unexpected demand this month has driven cash well-above index.

Traders said some buyers went into October short gas, expecting mild temperatures to keep demand slack. Forecasts for cool Midwest and East Coast weather this week and more heat out West triggered a scramble for incremental supply.
In addition, steady storage demand this month helped drive Gulf Caost swing prices almost 50 cents above index.
A Reuter poll showed expectations for a build in Wednesday's weekly AGA storage report averaged 70-75 bcf compared to a 48 bcf gain seen the same week last year.

Technically, traders said follow-through buying after yesterday's strong close and the break of near resistance again today set off more short covering and new buying. Last week's break of a head-and-shoulders bottom formation projects November prices into the $2.60s, but some said the market was overbought and could correct ahead of the weekly stock data later today. November support was seen around $2.30.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices jumped more than 10 cents today to about the $2.30 mark. Midcon pipes were up almost 15 cents to the high-teens. Gas at the New York city gate was pegged at about $2.60, also up more than a dime.
NYMEX said 33,048 Hub contracts traded at 1340 EDT.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas firmed two cents to $1.105, while deferreds were 1.5 to three cents higher. NYMEX said 144 Alberta contracts traded at 1340 EDT.
NYMEX Permian natgas was still untraded at 1415 EDT, but November remained bid six cents higher at $2.11.
On the KCBT, November was 11 cents higher at $2.26, while deferreds were up by four to seven cents. The East/West spread widened by 3.7 cents to 32.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
